scope: Independent source and test-design review only; no test execution, CI dispatch, VM, production, account, provider, or ref operation.

candidateBase.message:
Merge PR1835 source for combined issue1512 validation

Preserve the shared Claude certificate-policy fix and its tests in normal merge history. Original control receipts, the upstream owner's merge, full candidate CI and production acceptance remain separate completion requirements.

supersededDrafts.reason: Final ec849 changes two comment lines only; executable code unchanged.
Final 47ef appends one fixed-revision three-to-one SQL assertion; preceding 22 cases retained.

evidence: app/actions/coordinator.ts:47-82 authenticates the session, validates bot/workspace UUIDs, calls loadWorkspaceContext, rejects an expected-workspace mismatch before Coordinator creation, and queries bot by exact id/owner/workspace.

Only lines 101 and 134 wrap coordinatorEnabled; authorization remains outside and before the new lifetime. Chat state, revision, continuation, singleFlight key, and refresh authorization remain unchanged.
lib/workspace-access.ts:42-98 checks transport/PAT workspace selection and active membership. Supplied inaccessible selection does not fall back to a personal workspace.
coordinatorEnabled in lib/coordinator/wake.ts is unchanged; execution/wake callers do not receive the new wrapper.
lib/coordinator/model-ready.ts:13-31 resolves the exact bot workspace and calls the read-only preference/choice readers.
lib/bot-model-choice.ts:35-137 reads preferences and usable model choices, without saving a preference or cloning a binding.

The memoized value is only memberSubscriptionsAllowed, a workspace-level boolean. usableApiKeys retains owner-specific key reads; pooledOwners retains share reads; ExecutionSettings.sharedOwners retains separate active-membership authorization for both consumer and each shared owner.
Credential opening, reservation, othersMayUse, and runMayUseCredentialSql were not changed or newly wrapped.
Final read-batch-context.ts:26-30 opens a standalone AsyncLocalStorage observation only when no active Native batch/observation exists and the effective route is not after:/cron:/workflow:.
Policy memo identity is actual COMMIT_EXECUTOR or database object, followed by exact workspaceId. There is no cached user, membership result, credential, or provider output.
Success and rejection both execute finally, mark the scope inactive, and clear the map. Bound callbacks surviving the read cannot continue using that observation.
Within an existing Native batch, the original batch observation retains priority.

The existing production beginWorkspaceListRead callers are readTaskRuns and readThreads in app/actions/task-runs.ts. Both authenticate and await loadWorkspaceContext before this helper and before business-data queries.

The new plan is the intersection of the already prepared batch action names with three fixed mappings: issues.syncIssueList->issue_list, task-runs.pollTaskRuns->task_run_list, task-runs.syncThreadList->thread_list.
The helper requires a valid exact workspace ID and an originally requested matching planned kind:id before starting the plan. It cannot infer a Team from a personal-home result.
Entity reads, null or invalid scopes, mismatched refs, and unplanned kinds do not trigger the workspace union. Extra prefetched keys are filtered from each caller's result.
Authorization remains the caller's responsibility; this helper is not a membership-admission API and the new DB test explicitly says so.
Final revision map type is Map<object,RevisionQueue>; the suggested Map<Database>/object TS2345 problem is absent from the reviewed final bytes.
lib/db/request-scope.ts COMMIT_EXECUTOR returns heldClient, requestDatabase.pool, or default target, so distinct actual databases/clients behind the same exported proxy do not share observations.

Each pending queue is created under that executor and queueMicrotask is registered within the originating AsyncLocalStorage context. The query continues through the original database/proxy in that captured context.

captureDatabaseQuery retains its actual executor and bound request context; deviceScopedPool still wraps actual query execution. No new device-authority bypass or identity-switching call site was introduced.
Owner is not an extra revision-cache dimension because the cached value is only a workspace/entity revision counter; each business action independently retains its own owner/membership predicate.

The original per-key promise retains the first observed revision for the active batch, and callers still await it before reading data. Later consumers can receive an older version, never a version observed after their data.
Both owner-home and selected-workspace paths filter to the caller's requested keys and keep separate kind:id entries.
Revision SQL only returns safe positive integers for requested valid pairs. Missing rows do not become zero; errors propagate to beginWorkspaceListRead, which returns an empty revision object.
Inactive batch or effective after:/cron:/workflow: workspace reads use readLiveRevisions directly and do not inherit the plan.
No after-COMMIT writer target, ownerLiveScope fresh reader, or business-data query is changed.
personal-policy.test.ts uses a namespace lookup and falls back to directly invoking the old real consumers when withReadOnlyPolicyObservation is absent.
read-batch-context.test.ts and the DB test fall back to the actual old readBatchRevisions, so old source reaches behavior assertions instead of failing on a missing named export.
All three test diffs are additions only; old test bodies and assertions are retained.
The appended fixed-revision unit case first finishes three reads and checks exact original key/value results, then asserts one SQL call. Old behavior reaches this assertion with three calls.
The DB test executes actual readLiveRevisions SQL against three initialized counters and separately records result JSON bytes; it is not a wire/TLS byte measurement or a membership fixture.
Only four product modules and three directly related test files differ from the fixed base.
No Native harness, SQL counter, source-wordlist, checkpoint, budget, read window, live timing, polling interval, schema, dependency, provider, or worker source was modified by these seven blobs.
A does not claim to reduce the previous FIRST pair: both prior FIRST chat reads already had a Native batch observation. A's intended scope is later standalone chat readiness reads.
B's helper cost proof cannot be substituted for a complete real Native paired-window budget result.

Implementation receipt preserves the prior actual budget failure (full Native 433 versus Web 431; FIRST 209 versus hosted 147) without moving windows; this review has not reread those lifecycle originals.

initialB22.failureBoundary: Behavioral revision/executor/background assertions, not import failure; first Team case failed earlier on 12 versus 7, before its SQL-count assertion.

limitations: The policy memo intentionally holds one bounded observation of a workspace-level flag; it does not provide an atomic snapshot of all authorization or data reads.

Guard behavior is based on the effective currentRoute. Known execution/wake/after/cron/workflow callers were not newly wrapped; this review does not claim arbitrary future nested call sites automatically retain an overwritten route label.
The DB regression creates revision rows and passes an already authorized scope; admission safety is established here by source order at the real caller, not by that helper fixture.
Test-only local cost reductions, full canonical CI, and actual Native budget acceptance are separate evidence.
Any source blob change invalidates this exact-byte review for the changed path.
